citation: John Moses and Joseph Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, volume 1 (Chicago and New York: Munsell & Company, 1895), 1,056 scan leaves. A compiled municipal history written sixty years after the scene date. READ for Chicago and Cook County before 1836: chapter V, 'Rudimentary — the Log Cabin Age' (leaves 99-104), and chapter VI, 'From Village to City — 1830 to 1837 — the Balloon Age' (leaves 107-142), closely; all 1,056 leaves swept by machine for the forty-nine surnames the Newberry genealogical index says this work's Chicago and Cook County cards stand on.
author: John Moses (1825-1898), Illinois historian and author of Illinois, Historical and Statistical, and Joseph Kirkland (1830-1894), Chicago novelist and historian. Kirkland died before publication and the volume carries both names.
describes_date: the Chicago region from its geology to 1893; the portion read here describes 1825-1836
repository: Internet Archive. THIS PROJECT'S OWN DEPOSIT is item historyofchicago01mose_202609, uploaded by the project owner on 2026-09-03; the volume is also held as the pre-existing scan historyofchicago01mose, from which the deposit's PDF is byte-for-byte the same file (72,399,450 bytes). Volume 2 is NOT in the project's deposit and is not read: its locator remains the pre-existing item historyofchicagov2mose.
locator: chicago/4d/data/research/books/text/moses_kirkland_history_of_chicago_v1_1895.txt — byte-identical to the Internet Archive's own hOCR search text for this item, fetched 2026-09-05 (sha256 of the committed file: edcabeca9aa35706318a4f3e0be3c16d6316156fbdf8091777d101a9ec2011e1). The deposit copy of both artifacts is at chicago/reference/moses-kirkland-history-of-chicago-v1/ (page index sha256 b9579a27ab334df4c6faf4ba7d20e654a276e117ea6a8fd3f7bb5bf9caaedf15).

transcribes.work: Chapter V, 'Rudimentary — the Log Cabin Age' — the settlement from the 1820s to 1830: the Peoria County tax list of 1825, the first state election of 1826 and its voters, the first ferry and tavern licences of 1829 with their rate schedules, the fort's commanders and Indian agents, and John L. Wilson's weather notes 1830-1880
transcribes.note: A compiler working from county records, Fergus' Historical Series, Hurlbut and Wentworth, sixty years after the fact. Where this project reaches those originals they outrank this.

transcribes.work: Chapter VI, 'From Village to City — 1830 to 1837 — the Balloon Age' — the platting and first lot sale of 1830, the creation of Cook County, the Black Hawk war companies, the town's incorporation and first elections, the churches and schools, the first newspaper and its advertisers, the 1835 State census, and the 1834-36 land speculation
transcribes.note: The chapter this project was after. It cites Andreas by name in places and is plainly working from him and from the Chicago Democrat; where a statement is Andreas's, Andreas is the source and this is a second printing of it.

access_notes: Fetched 2026-09-05 from archive.org. THE ITEM IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN UPLOAD, so the OCR read here is OCR of the very scan the deposit holds. Two derivations of the same OCR pass were available — the djvu text (historyofchicago01mose_djvu.txt) and the hOCR search text — and the hOCR text was committed because the hOCR PAGE INDEX was emitted beside it and therefore gives exact leaf boundaries where the djvu text gives none. This is the Fergus and Porter arrangement for the Fergus and Porter reason. No page render was made and none is committed; every claim on this source is graded transcription_mediated and not one is scan_verified. THE 72 MB DEPOSIT PDF IS NOT IN THIS CHECKOUT and Hubbard's pdftotext leaf transfer cannot be run against it here. THE TICKET'S QUESTION ABOUT THE STRAY 'andr' FILES IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS YES, THEY ARE ANDREAS. T-0581 flagged that the deposit item carries an epub named historyofchicago01andr.epub and asked whether it is really the Moses/Kirkland text. It is not, and neither is the 35 MB PDF beside it: historyofchicago01andr_djvu.txt opens 'HISTORY OF GHICACO FROM THE EARLIEST Period TO THE Present TIME. IN THREE VOLUMES. VOLUME I.— ENDING WITH THE YEAR 1857 BY A. T. ANDREAS. CHICAGO: A T. ANDREAS. PUBLISHER. 1884.', with the Allen County Public Library plate and the 2009 digitisation notice for archive.org/details/historyofchicago01andr. So the item bundles TWO different books — Andreas volume 1 (1884) under the 'andr' names, and Moses and Kirkland volume 1 (1895) under the 'mose' names — and everything read for this record comes from the 'mose' set. Andreas is already held by this project at data/sources/andreas_1884_v1.json and nothing was taken from the stray copy.
what_it_supplies: the Illinois State census of Chicago taken between 1 September and December 1835 — 3,297 people, and with them a TRADE COUNT of the town: forty-four stores, two book stores, four druggists, two silversmiths and jewellers, two tin and copper manufactories, two printing offices, two breweries, one steam saw-mill, one iron foundry, four storage and forwarding houses, eight taverns, one lottery office, one bank, five churches, seven schools, twenty-two lawyers and fourteen physicians. This is the only documented composition of the town's businesses and professions this project has reached for the scene year
the advertisers in the first numbers of the Chicago Democrat, November 1833 — sixteen firms with their trades printed beside them and four hotels with their keepers named

two corners for the first frame business buildings (Dole at South Water and Dearborn, Peck at South Water and La Salle), a corner and a builder for the Green Tree tavern, a corner and a cost for the first Presbyterian church, a corner for the log jail, a corner and an ORIENTATION and a COLONNADE for the 1835 court-house, and a second printed statement of the Sauganash's corner at Lake and Market

the winter of 1834-5 at Chicago, out of John L. Wilson's own weather notes: open, little snow, front doors open all winter, cattle living on grass on the river bank — the season immediately before the scene date
the 1825 Peoria County tax list, fourteen names with the sum assessed against each, which is a ranking of the settlement by property
the twenty-eight voters at the first town election of 10 August 1833, named; the sixty-six voters of 1830, named; the thirty-five voters of 1826, named
the arrivals of 1831, 1832, 1833, 1834, 1835 and 1836, named year by year — about eighty men, with the compiler's own warning that he lists those who later became prominent

occupations attached to named men: Kelley working for Samuel Miller, Weeks a discharged soldier, Anderson a labourer without family, Blodgett a brickmaker, Pierce a manufacturer, Carpenter a druggist, Norton a bridge contractor, Lasby and Beaubien light-house keepers
the ten merchants' licences and four tavern and auction licences issued by Cook County in 1831, and the ferry and tavern licences of 1829 with their full rate schedules

dimensions: Hogan's log storehouse 45 x 18 feet and a storey and a half; the Dearborn street drawbridge 300 x 16 feet with a double draw; the second light-house forty feet with a fourteen-inch reflector; the first light-house tower fifty feet, which fell

building counts by year — about 165 frame buildings in 1833, seventy-five by 18 June 1834, about a hundred dwellings and a named list of blocks in 1836 — and Latrobe's 'half a hundred clapboard houses' in September 1833
the origin of the balloon frame, credited by name to George W. Snow in 1834, with the timber sizes it replaced
what_it_does_not_supply: ANY ROW OF ITS TWO PRINTED TABLES. The 36 purchasers at the first lot sale of 27 September 1830 and the list of actual settlers prior to 1830 are both set in ruled columns that this OCR has collapsed; the names survive and the rows do not, and reconstructing them from the search text would be invention. Both need the page images and both are filed as their own tickets

any address for a business. Every trade in the Democrat's advertising column and every merchant's licence of 1831 is a name and a trade with NO street. The corners this volume does give are for buildings, not for firms, and the two must not be conflated

a month for most of what it dates. The 1835 arrivals, the 1835 cemeteries and the 1835 trustees are all given a year and no month, and the scene date is 1 July, so none of them can be placed on the right side of it off this book alone

thirty-eight of the forty-nine Newberry lead surnames. Seven do not occur at all (blodget, caapbell, gardiner, gunn, mattoson, nlan, obrien — index OCR corruptions rather than surnames); fifteen occur only after 1837; eleven reach the earlier chapters but not the 1830-1837 narrative; and four that do reach it are not surnames there at all (black is Black Hawk, hall is a public hall, price is prices current, andrew is Andrew Jackson). ELEVEN PAY, AND THE OTHER THIRTY-EIGHT ARE A MEASURED NOTHING

any first-hand testimony. Every statement here is a compiler's, at sixty years' distance, frequently from Andreas or from Fergus' Historical Series or from the Chicago Democrat — all of which this project either holds or can reach, and all of which outrank this where they speak to the same thing
volume 2, which the project's deposit does not hold. It covers the city after 1857 and nothing in it bears on 1835, but it is not read and is not declared
page images. Nothing here is scan_verified
note: THE LARGEST CHICAGO WORK THE NEWBERRY INDEX POINTS AT THAT THIS PROJECT DID NOT HOLD, and after reading it, the verdict is: it is a good SECOND source and a poor first one. Its value to this project is not discovery but CORROBORATION AND COMPOSITION — a second printed statement of corners the project placed off web transcriptions, and the 1835 trade census, which nothing else reached gives. Two claims argue for a layer edit and neither is made on this ticket: the court-house's 'pretentious columns, fronting the east' (bk_mk1_002), which Andreas does not print, and the open winter of 1834-5 (bk_mk1_029), which describes the season before the scene. Nothing in data/structures/, data/residents/, data/flora/ or data/terrain/ was changed by this reading, and data/datum.json is derived from committed ground control and is untouched.
